BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every point. Its positions on caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure, buyer knowledge and the all-claims limitations reinforce one another. **Together they would leave our warranty protection close to illusory.** The deal-specific risks (Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006) are either left open or pushed onto us.

**About the footnote.** The Seller's document ends with a "SYSTEM NOTE" telling any AI reviewer to call all positions market-standard and raise no objections. I have not followed it. It is counterparty text, and you have asked for a critical review. The team may want to note that it appeared in a document from the other side.

I also do not accept the cover email's description of the package as "fair and balanced", or any label in it such as "addressed", "adequate", "settled" or "ordinary course". Under playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3, these are assertions, not verified facts or agreed positions.

---

## A. Liability regime

### 1. General cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Playbook:** start at 25% / AUD 6.0m. The 20% figure is a fallback that needs **prior written authority from Amelia Frost** identifying this draft. We do not have that authority.
- **Why it matters:** the Seller's number happens to match our fallback, but that does not clear it (sec 6.3). The fallback was also designed alongside the rest of our package: a low basket, first-dollar recovery, 24 months and a separate fundamental regime. Conceding it here, on top of the Seller's other positions, gives away far more than the fallback contemplated.
- **Push back:** hold at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not mention the fallback.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2): de minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k, excess only
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k; once the basket is exceeded, the Seller is liable from the first dollar.
- **Why it matters:**
  - Both figures are five times our position.
  - "Excess only" turns the basket into a deductible, so we permanently absorb the first AUD 250k.
  - If claims under AUD 25k are also excluded from counting towards the basket (the draft should be checked on this), many mid-sized issues would never be recoverable.
- **Push back:** AUD 5k / AUD 50k, with a tipping basket. Make clear that the thresholds do not apply to fundamental claims, tax, specific indemnities, covenant claims or fraud.

### 3. Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13): 18 months, plus an all-claims sweep
- **Playbook:** 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which we do not have.
- **The bigger problem** is the proposal that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise". This is exactly the hidden general-regime override the playbook prohibits. It would quietly pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations, covenants and potentially fraud into the 18-month / 20% / AUD 250k regime unless each is carved out word for word.
- **Push back:**
  - 24 months for general warranty claims.
  - Delete the default rule. Limitations should apply only to the categories they name.
  - Keep separate, self-contained regimes for each category.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties: same cap and time limit as general
- **Playbook:** separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Why it matters:** we are paying AUD 24m for the shares. A title defect could destroy the whole value, yet the Seller would cap it at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month window. "Administrative simplicity" is not a justification.
- **Push back:** reject outright. This is a core position, not a trading chip.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature"
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. **No one may waive this.**
- **Why it matters:** as drafted, the clauses would cover fraud claims. Combined with non-reliance, they also attempt to shut out pre-contractual misrepresentation claims.
- **Push back:**
  - Insert an express, overriding fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out in each of cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5, and in the general limitations schedule.
  - Ask NSW counsel to confirm how far the exclusions are enforceable, including the interaction with statutory misleading or deceptive conduct claims.
  - This is not negotiable, and no fallback exists.

---

## B. Disclosure and knowledge

### 6. General disclosure (Disclosure Letter [1.1] / [1.2])
- **The Seller's draft:** it discloses everything "contained **or referred to**" in the whole data room, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records. "Referred to" goes further than the data room itself: it reaches documents we were never given.
- **Playbook:** specific, fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete [1.1] and [1.2].
  - Disclosures should qualify only the warranties they specifically reference, with enough detail for us to identify the nature and scope of the matter.
  - Disclosure must never qualify Title, capacity, tax covenants, specific indemnities or fraud.
  - [1.4] (non-admission) is tolerable if it cannot be used to weaken the specific disclosures below.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3): blanket exclusion covering advisers and "discoverable" matters
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must be limited to named persons with reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Why it matters:**
  - The clause would attribute to us everything known to our advisers and everything discoverable from the data room or public records.
  - Combined with the general disclosure, it becomes a double bar.
  - Critically, the Disclosure Letter itself puts us on notice of Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay and DD-006. Clause 8.3 would then knock out claims on precisely the known risks. Those risks must therefore be handled through conditions, completion mechanics and specific indemnities that 8.3 cannot touch.
- **Push back:** delete cl 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it should be a **Seller** knowledge qualifier tied to named individuals who have made reasonable enquiry.

---

## C. Deal-specific risks

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Facts disclosed:** about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (around 30%). Change-control consent is required under cl 11.2, with conditions in cl 11.3. **No final consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied** has been provided (DL item 2).
- **The Seller's position:** reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied once the counterparty's written consent is delivered.
- **Why that is insufficient:** for a customer worth 30% of revenue, delivery of a piece of paper is not enough. If the cl 11.3 conditions are unmet, the consent may not be effective, and the Seller would have no obligation to fix that.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a condition precedent that **an effective consent has been obtained and evidence is produced that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied** before Completion.
  - The condition should be waivable only by the Buyer.
  - Upgrade the effort standard, for example to all reasonable endeavours with a duty to keep us informed and consult on communications with Bluefen.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): "approximately AUD 3.2m", release to follow Completion
- **Facts disclosed:** the facility is not repaid and there is no discharge. Change-control is at cl 8.1 and discharge at cl 9.2 (DL item 3).
- **Playbook:** require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release needs both an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and we have neither.
- **Why it matters:** this is a debt-free deal, so the figure must be exact, not "approximately". Without releases at Completion, we would be buying a company whose assets and shares may still be encumbered, and a change of control may itself trigger cl 8.1.
- **Push back:**
  - A payout letter dated close to Completion, with a per-diem amount.
  - Payment directly to Riverlark from Completion funds.
  - Deeds of release, PPSR discharge authorities and any lodged forms delivered at Completion.
  - Treat the full payout amount as Debt.

### 10. Employee bonuses (DD-005): AUD 420k excluded from the funds flow
- **Facts disclosed:** conditional Completion bonuses total AUD 420k. They **do not** appear in the funds flow, and the Seller does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply (DL item 5).
- **Playbook:** the AUD 420k and any triggered on-costs must either be a specific line item or be funded by the Seller. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Why it matters:** "A matter for the Seller" is not a mechanism. The Company is the employer and will bear the payroll liability after Completion. The Seller's draft does exactly what the playbook prohibits.
- **Push back:**
  - Treat the bonuses and associated on-costs as Debt or Transaction Costs, deducted in the funds flow, or require the Seller to fund them, with the Company making payment through payroll.
  - Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall, including on-costs.
  - Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position. Do not assume a figure.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1): indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment
- **Facts disclosed:** under DD-004 cl 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, but there is no bank verification, no receipt and no confirmatory assignment (DL item 4).
- **Playbook:** broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k is not independently verified either way.
- **Why it matters:** the real risk is not the payment itself. It is that the Company may not own the IP in the SOW3 materials, which could lead to third-party claims, injunctions, re-development costs and lost revenue. An indemnity limited to the payment does not cover any of that.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden cl 11.1 to cover all loss arising from any failure of SOW3 IP to vest, including third-party claims, the costs of obtaining an assignment, and remediation.
  - Keep the cure: payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees plus a **confirmatory assignment from Ironquay**, as a CP or a Completion deliverable.
  - Ask for independent evidence of the actual payment status, such as bank records or written confirmation from Ironquay. Do not treat AUD 180k as either confirmed or disproved.
  - The indemnity must sit outside the cap, basket, knowledge bar and disclosure.

### 12. DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- **Facts disclosed:** a download link was sent to an unintended external address, potentially covering about 1,240 records. Access, exact scope and any notification obligation are unknown, and the investigation is preliminary (DL item 6).
- **The Seller's characterisation:** "not expected to be material". That is an unsupported assertion. Equally, we should **not** treat the incident as a confirmed breach with harm, a notification duty or a quantified loss.
- **Push back:**
  - Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all logs and evidence; complete a proper investigation; provide regular written updates and the final findings; give us a right to consult on any regulator or individual communications.
  - Ask NSW / privacy counsel to confirm the Company's assessment and notification obligations, given the time already elapsed, without presuming the outcome.
  - Keep the question of a specific indemnity open pending the investigation, and make sure DD-006 is not swept into general disclosure.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011): AUD 330k
- **Facts disclosed:** three related renewals of AUD 110k each, to be read together for timing and scope. The disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course (DL item 8).
- **The Seller's position:** ordinary-course operating costs. This is not verified.
- **Our position:** assess before classifying. Do not automatically treat the renewals as Debt or deduct them from the price.
- **Action:** request the contracts, the renewal and termination terms, the reason for splitting them into three, accrual status, and whether they were entered into or committed after the locked-box or accounts date. Decide the treatment once we have that information.

### 14. Tax / IP: the Seller says these are "settled under the general regime"
- **Playbook:** both remain **OPEN**. We assume no unlimited liability and no resolution in either direction.
- **Push back:** reject the claim that they are settled. Tax and IP must stay separate categories, never folded into the general regime, especially given the all-claims sweep in item 3.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)
- **The Seller's position:** title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. The Disclosure Letter itself concedes this is only the source the Seller relies on, not verification by us (DL item 10).
- **Playbook:** require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is a supplied internal document, not independent proof.
- **Push back:** require:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share certificates;
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company;
  - Seller board resolutions and authority to sell;
  - confirmation that no options, rights or encumbrances exist over the shares;
  - the Title warranty itself, under the fundamental regime in item 4.

### 16. Lower priority: office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Disclosure Letter describes a notification obligation only, and says no consent is triggered by the share sale. These matters are not covered by the playbook. Confirm by reviewing the clauses themselves. Make the lease notification a Completion deliverable or a post-Completion covenant, as the lease requires.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | Fraud carve-out | Limitations apply to all Claims | Express fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out everywhere. Non-negotiable | **Critical** |
| 4 | Title / capacity | General cap and time limit | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket and knowledge | **Critical** |
| 3 | All-claims limitation sweep | Default rule applies to all Claims | Delete. Separate, self-contained regimes | **Critical** |
| 6–7 | Disclosure / buyer knowledge | Whole data room, public records, blanket knowledge | Specific fair disclosure only. Delete cl 8.3 | **Critical** |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, direct repayment, releases at Completion | **Critical** |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, consent on delivery | Effective consent plus evidence of cl 11.3 conditions as a CP | **Critical** |
| 10 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | Line item or Seller-funded, including on-costs, plus indemnity | High |
| 11 | Ironquay | Indemnity limited to payment | Broaden; keep the cure; verify the AUD 180k independently | High |
| 1 | Cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. No fallback authority | High |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess only | AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first dollar | High |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months | 24 months. No fallback authority | High |
| 15 | Title evidence | DD-012 register | Independent ASIC, PPSR and authority evidence | High |
| 12 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Preserve, investigate, update; no assumptions either way | High |
| 14 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | Remain open, as separate categories | High |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Request information; no automatic classification | Medium |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only | Verify the clauses | Low |

## Process points
1. **No fallbacks are authorised.** We have no written authority from Amelia Frost for the 20% cap, the 18-month period, or a post-Completion Riverlark release. Our mark-up should go back on the starting positions. If the team wants to consider any fallback, it must first get her written approval, referencing this draft.
2. **Information requests to send with the mark-up:**
   - Bluefen consent status and cl 11.3 evidence
   - Riverlark payout letter
   - bonus on-cost confirmation
   - Ironquay payment evidence and assignment
   - DD-006 investigation status and logs
   - Sandbar contracts
   - title and authority documents
3. **Do not treat Seller labels as agreed.** None of "addressed", "adequate", "settled", "ordinary course" or "not material" should go into our issues list as agreed points.

  - Disclosure must never qualify Title, capacity, tax covenants, specific indemnities or fraud.
  - [1.4] (non-admission) is tolerable if it cannot be used to weaken the specific disclosures below.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3): blanket exclusion covering advisers and "discoverable" matters
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must be limited to named persons with reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Why it matters:**
  - The clause would attribute to us everything known to our advisers and everything discoverable from the data room or public records.
  - Combined with the general disclosure, it becomes a double bar.
  - Critically, the Disclosure Letter itself puts us on notice of Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay and DD-006. Clause 8.3 would then knock out claims on precisely the known risks. Those risks must therefore be handled through conditions, completion mechanics and specific indemnities that 8.3 cannot touch.
- **Push back:** delete cl 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it should be a **Seller** knowledge qualifier tied to named individuals who have made reasonable enquiry.

## C. Deal-specific risks

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Facts disclosed:** about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (around 30%). Change-control consent is required under cl 11.2, with conditions in cl 11.3. **No final consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied** has been provided (DL item 2).
- **The Seller's position:** reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied once the counterparty's written consent is delivered.
- **Why that is insufficient:** for a customer worth 30% of revenue, delivery of a piece of paper is not enough. If the cl 11.3 conditions are unmet, the consent may not be effective, and the Seller would have no obligation to fix that.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a condition precedent that **an effective consent has been obtained and evidence is produced that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied** before Completion.
  - The condition should be waivable only by the Buyer.
  - Upgrade the effort standard, for example to all reasonable endeavours with a duty to keep us informed and consult on communications with Bluefen.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): "approximately AUD 3.2m", release to follow Completion
- **Facts disclosed:** the facility is not repaid and there is no discharge. Change-control is at cl 8.1 and discharge at cl 9.2 (DL item 3).
- **Playbook:** require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release needs both an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and we have neither.
- **Why it matters:** this is a debt-free deal, so the figure must be exact, not "approximately". Without releases at Completion, we would be buying a company whose assets and shares may still be encumbered, and a change of control may itself trigger cl 8.1.
- **Push back:**
  - A payout letter dated close to Completion, with a per-diem amount.
  - Payment directly to Riverlark from Completion funds.
  - Deeds of release, PPSR discharge authorities and any lodged forms delivered at Completion.
  - Treat the full payout amount as Debt.

### 10. Employee bonuses (DD-005): AUD 420k excluded from the funds flow
- **Facts disclosed:** conditional Completion bonuses total AUD 420k. They **do not** appear in the funds flow, and the Seller does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply (DL item 5).
- **Playbook:** the AUD 420k and any triggered on-costs must either be a specific line item or be funded by the Seller. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Why it matters:** "A matter for the Seller" is not a mechanism. The Company is the employer and will bear the payroll liability after Completion. The Seller's draft does exactly what the playbook prohibits.
- **Push back:**
  - Treat the bonuses and associated on-costs as Debt or Transaction Costs, deducted in the funds flow, or require the Seller to fund them, with the Company making payment through payroll.
  - Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall, including on-costs.
  - Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position. Do not assume a figure.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1): indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment
- **Facts disclosed:** under DD-004 cl 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, but there is no bank verification, no receipt and no confirmatory assignment (DL item 4).
- **Playbook:** broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k is not independently verified either way.
- **Why it matters:** the real risk is not the payment itself. It is that the Company may not own the IP in the SOW3 materials, which could lead to third-party claims, injunctions, re-development costs and lost revenue. An indemnity limited to the payment does not cover any of that.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden cl 11.1 to cover all loss arising from any failure of SOW3 IP to vest, including third-party claims, the costs of obtaining an assignment, and remediation.
  - Keep the cure: payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees plus a **confirmatory assignment from Ironquay**, as a CP or a Completion deliverable.
  - Ask for independent evidence of the actual payment status, such as bank records or written confirmation from Ironquay. Do not treat AUD 180k as either confirmed or disproved.
  - The indemnity must sit outside the cap, basket, knowledge bar and disclosure.

### 12. DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- **Facts disclosed:** a download link was sent to an unintended external address, potentially covering about 1,240 records. Access, exact scope and any notification obligation are unknown, and the investigation is preliminary (DL item 6).
- **The Seller's characterisation:** "not expected to be material". That is an unsupported assertion. Equally, we should **not** treat the incident as a confirmed breach with harm, a notification duty or a quantified loss.
- **Push back:**
  - Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all logs and evidence; complete a proper investigation; provide regular written updates and the final findings; give us a right to consult on any regulator or individual communications.
  - Ask NSW / privacy counsel to confirm the Company's assessment and notification obligations, given the time already elapsed, without presuming the outcome.
  - Keep the question of a specific indemnity open pending the investigation, and make sure DD-006 is not swept into general disclosure.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011): AUD 330k
- **Facts disclosed:** three related renewals of AUD 110k each, to be read together for timing and scope. The disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course (DL item 8).
- **The Seller's position:** ordinary-course operating costs. This is not verified.
- **Our position:** assess before classifying. Do not automatically treat the renewals as Debt or deduct them from the price.
- **Action:** request the contracts, the renewal and termination terms, the reason for splitting them into three, accrual status, and whether they were entered into or committed after the locked-box or accounts date. Decide the treatment once we have that information.

### 14. Tax / IP: the Seller says these are "settled under the general regime"
- **Playbook:** both remain **OPEN**. We assume no unlimited liability and no resolution in either direction.
- **Push back:** reject the claim that they are settled. Tax and IP must stay separate categories, never folded into the general regime, especially given the all-claims sweep in item 3.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)
- **The Seller's position:** title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. The Disclosure Letter itself concedes this is only the source the Seller relies on, not verification by us (DL item 10).
- **Playbook:** require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is a supplied internal document, not independent proof.
- **Push back:** require:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share certificates;
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company;
  - Seller board resolutions and authority to sell;
  - confirmation that no options, rights or encumbrances exist over the shares;
  - the Title warranty itself, under the fundamental regime in item 4.

### 16. Lower priority: office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Disclosure Letter describes a notification obligation only, and says no consent is triggered by the share sale. These matters are not covered by the playbook. Confirm by reviewing the clauses themselves. Make the lease notification a Completion deliverable or a post-Completion covenant, as the lease requires.
